hero.sede: Panda Troupe, Olivera, Buenos Aires, Argentina

parrafos: For the first time, Argentina is hosting the Latin American Bowhunter Championship. From December 5th to 8th, archers from across the region will gather at Panda Troupe, a former quarry turned woodland: uneven ground, shadows, demanding angles, and silhouettes cutting through the trees.

Four days of competition under IFAA rules, where good aim alone isn't enough. You have to read the terrain, judge every distance, and trust your instinct. A course designed to challenge the best 3D archers in Latin America in a uniquely natural setting.
But LABHC is also a gathering. Four days to bring the community together, share an asado, swap experiences with archers from different countries, and celebrate a discipline that keeps on growing.
Whatever your 3D background, your bow has a place here. We'll be waiting for you in the woods, from December 5th to 8th.

bloque1.titulo: The union of Flechar and Liga 3D Metropolitana
parrafos: Liga 3D Metropolitana and Club Flechar were born from the same place: a passion for 3D archery and the drive to help it grow. Over four consecutive years, L3DM established itself by organizing the country's best 3D tournaments, bringing together a community of hundreds of archers of every level, awarding millions of pesos in prizes, and setting up Argentina's best 3D targets on the range.

Flechar, an archery school with more than two decades of experience, brings the pillar that any top-level competition needs: technical knowledge. Its IFAA international instructor certification and its experience training archers add the sporting rigor, teaching, and command of the rulebook that make the difference.

Joining these two forces wasn't a coincidence — it was the natural conclusion of two institutions that share the same vision: that Argentine 3D archery deserves to stand alongside the best in the world.

That union gave rise to the most ambitious challenge the community has ever taken on: organizing, for the first time in Argentina, the Latin American Bowhunter Championship. This isn't just a tournament — it's the most important 3D event in Argentine history: a chance to put the country on the continental map of the discipline, and to show, both at home and abroad, everything we're capable of building when we work together.
It's a big bet, with little time and a lot to do, but taken on with the conviction that we're writing a page Argentine 3D archery will remember.

The IFAA (International Field Archery Association) is the international association that brings together field and bowhunter archery. Founded in 1970 by archers from the United States, Sweden, England, Scotland, Wales, and Canada, it now brings together more than 50,000 archers in 45 countries across every continent. It is also a member of TAFISA (The Association for International Sport for All), the world body for "sport for all" recognized by the International Olympic Committee.

Unlike World Archery — the Olympic federation most Argentine archers know — the IFAA was born out of field and bowhunter archery, in close contact with nature. Its spirit is different: courses set on natural terrain, distances that often have to be judged by eye, a wide variety of bow styles, and a system of classes and divisions that lets both amateurs and professionals compete, whatever their level. Its formats range from field — with marked distances and paper targets — to bowhunter (3D) — animal silhouettes at unknown distances — plus indoor shooting.

The IFAA organizes the world championships and sanctions the annual championships of its six regions, one of which is Latin America. The Latin American Bowhunter Championship is precisely that: our region's championship — having the IFAA's endorsement is what gives this tournament its official, Latin American standing.

bloque3.intro: The Latin American Bowhunter Championship 2026 is run by an organizing committee made up of four leading figures from Club Flechar and Liga 3D Metropolitana.

comite.bio: Director and founder of the Flechar Archery School (2003). World indoor archery champion (2009), multiple-time national champion, and South American champion in the discipline. National Physical Education Teacher, National archery coach, and IFAA International Instructor II. Over more than two decades he has trained hundreds of archers across Flechar's various locations, with notable work in adaptive and inclusive archery.

President of Liga 3D Metropolitana (L3DM) and archer at Club Atlético Independiente. Longbow shooter since 2011. He has taken part in four IFAA world championships: the World Bowhunter Championships in 2017 in Chianti (Italy), 2023 in Rovaniemi (Finland), and 2025 in South Africa, as well as the 2024 World Field Championships in Foz do Iguaçu (Brazil). He also competed in the 2018 IFAA South American Bowhunter Championship in Campos do Jordão (Brazil) and the 2019 World Archery South American 3D Championship in Paysandú (Uruguay).

Club Flechar. 2022 Latin American Indoor Championship winner. 2023 Latin American Field Archery Championship runner-up. 2025 indoor world runner-up. Multiple-time national champion across the different IFAA disciplines.

Secretary of the Asociación Civil de Tiro con Arco La Liga and archer at Club Atlético Independiente. Traditional bow shooter since 2019 and longbow shooter since 2026. He was part of the Argentine 3D national team at the Rinehart World Archery 3D Championship in Terni, Italy (2022) and at the World Championship in Mokrice, Slovenia (2024), and competed at the IFAA World Bowhunter Championship (WBHC 2025) in South Africa. Finalist for the Jorge Newbery Awards in the Archery category (2023). National and regional indoor champion (2023), national 3D runner-up (2023), and national IFAA Field runner-up (2026); regional and metropolitan outdoor champion (2021).
